witnesses.evidence: The text began »ἐν τῷ πεντεκαιδεκάτῳ ἔτει Τιβερίου Καίσαρος« καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς; 1:1–2:52, the baptism (3:21–22) and the genealogy (3:23–38) were not in it.
"Anno quintodecimo principatus Tiberiani proponit eum descendisse in civitatem Galilaeae Capharnaum" — the date and the descent to Capernaum stated as one sentence.
Marcion's Jesus came "temporibus Pontii Pilati praesidis, qui fuit procurator Tiberii Caesaris".

records.wording: NA27 without δέ. The opening δέ is absent from both witnesses (Epiphanius quotes the incipit without it; Tertullian "Anno quintodecimo"), and a book cannot open with a connective. The clauses naming Herod, Philip and Lysanias are unattested; NA27 is printed for them. The Pilate clause is attested in sense (Irenaeus); Roth reconstructs it as ἐπὶ τῶν χρόνων Ποντίου Πιλάτου (probable only), so NA27 is printed.

records.reason: The witnesses join the date of 3:1 directly to the descent to Capernaum (4:31): Tertullian 4.7.1 in one sentence; Irenaeus, Haer. 1.27.2 and Hippolytus, Haer. 7.31 likewise open with the descent. The sequence leaves no room for John's preaching. Roth classes 3:2–20 as unattested; the difference is recorded.
